AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. About how high should a compost heap be built? (1 mark)
   A. Only one hand high
   B. About as high as your chest
   C. As flat as the ground
   D. As high as a house

2. Why is a cloth placed over the opening of the water container? (1 mark)
   A. To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   B. To make the water hot
   C. To make the container heavier
   D. To colour the water

3. What is drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Flooding the whole field
   B. Spraying water high into the air
   C. Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
   D. Throwing water from a bucket quickly

4. Why is the water container placed on a stand? (1 mark)
   A. To keep it out of the sun forever
   B. To hide it from birds
   C. So it looks tall
   D. So water flows down through the pipe

5. What is the best time of day to water crops? (1 mark)
   A. Noon
   B. Early morning or late afternoon
   C. Midnight only
   D. Never

6. Which statement about a three-stone fire is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It loses a lot of heat to the air
   B. It saves the most fuel
   C. It is completely smoke-free
   D. It never needs firewood

7. Why does a lid on a pot save fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   B. It makes the pot lighter
   C. It stops the food from cooking
   D. It cools the food

8. What should the scarecrow pole be like? (1 mark)
   A. Made of glass
   B. Very short
   C. Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   D. Loose so it can fall over

9. Which is the best material for stuffing a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Stones
   C. Dry grass
   D. Wet mud

10. What is a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   B. A farm tool for digging
   C. A wild bird
   D. A kind of fence

11. What is poaching? (1 mark)
   A. Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   B. Watering crops
   C. Planting trees
   D. Feeding wild animals

12. What might a hungry hare eat in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Metal
   B. Glass
   C. Stones
   D. Young shoots of vegetables

13. How deep should tiny seeds be sown? (1 mark)
   A. About 1 cm
   B. About 30 cm
   C. As deep as a hand
   D. On top of a heap

14. Why should a seedbed for tiny seeds be fine? (1 mark)
   A. It is a school rule
   B. Lumps help seeds
   C. Fine soil makes seeds bigger
   D. Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps

15. Why do we mix tiny seeds with dry sand? (1 mark)
   A. To make them wet
   B. To spread them thinly and evenly
   C. To kill germs
   D. To make them heavy

16. Why is dry grass laid lightly over a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the soil hard
   B. It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   C. It stops seeds growing
   D. It makes seeds fly

17. Why do we weed around fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Weeds give fruits
   B. Weeds take water and food from the plants
   C. Weeds protect the stem
   D. Weeds add sugar

18. What is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal that lives freely in the forest
   B. An animal kept and cared for by people
   C. An animal that cannot be tamed
   D. An animal found only in parks

19. Which animal is kept mainly for wool? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Wool sheep
   C. Donkey
   D. Hen

20. What is the young one of a cow called? (1 mark)
   A. Chick
   B. Kid
   C. Calf
   D. Lamb

21. Why should raw milk be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. To make it thicker
   B. To kill germs
   C. To make it colder
   D. To make it blue

22. Which of these is an energy-giving fat? (1 mark)
   A. Beans
   B. Cooking oil
   C. Spinach
   D. Oranges

23. Which of these is a body-building food? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Chapati
   C. Rice
   D. Beans

24. Which of these fruits is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Orange
   B. Chapati
   C. Butter
   D. Rice

25. Which is a disadvantage of too much frying? (1 mark)
   A. Too much oil is not good for health
   B. It removes all flavour
   C. It uses no heat
   D. It makes food cold

26. Which of these is used for boiling food? (1 mark)
   A. A plate
   B. A frying pan only
   C. A saucepan with a lid
   D. A basket

27. Which disease can be spread by dirty hands? (1 mark)
   A. Toothache only
   B. Broken leg
   C. Diarrhoea
   D. Sunburn

28. What is the correct order for cleaning a room? (1 mark)
   A. Dust, sweep, mop
   B. Sweep, mop, dust
   C. Mop, dust, sweep
   D. Mop, sweep, dust

29. Which is recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Sending it to sea
   B. Burying it
   C. Turning used material into something new
   D. Burning it

30. Why is a damp cloth used for dusting? (1 mark)
   A. It hides dust
   B. It traps the dust
   C. It dries the room
   D. It scatters the dust

31. What should you wear when handling rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. Only a hat
   B. Gloves
   C. Nothing
   D. Sandals only

32. Which refuse can be put in the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bottles
   B. Vegetable peelings
   C. Tins
   D. Batteries

33. Where should canvas shoes be dried? (1 mark)
   A. In a sealed box
   B. In an airy, shady place
   C. In a fire
   D. Under wet clothes

34. Which is a correct step for cleaning gloves? (1 mark)
   A. Snatch them off by the fingers
   B. Wear them wet
   C. Pull them off from the wrist so the dirty outside does not touch skin
   D. Put them on again dirty

35. What should you do if your PPE is damaged? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it in a river
   B. Hide it
   C. Keep using it
   D. Tell a teacher or an adult

36. What should you do with cleaning materials afterwards? (1 mark)
   A. Give to animals
   B. Drink them
   C. Store them away from small children
   D. Leave them on the floor

37. Which cloth is easiest for beginners? (1 mark)
   A. Thick leather
   B. Wire mesh
   C. Slippery silk
   D. Cotton

38. What should you do if you prick your finger? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Put dirt on it
   C. Tell the teacher and wash with soap and water
   D. Hide it

39. Which item can be made with tacking stitches in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. A roof
   B. A handkerchief
   C. A house
   D. A car

40. Which tool holds a needle safely on the finger to push it? (1 mark)
   A. Thimble
   B. Scissors
   C. Ruler
   D. Pin cushion

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name three PPE items and what each protects. (3 marks)

42. Name three small wild animals that destroy crops. (3 marks)

43. Give two reasons why soil should be conserved. (2 marks)

44. How do fruits help our health? (3 marks)

45. How should cloth items such as overalls and cloth masks be cleaned? (3 marks)

46. Explain pruning. (2 marks)

47. Explain the meaning of domestic hygiene. (2 marks)

48. Describe how to make a bottle drip for one plant. (3 marks)

49. Give three uses of sheep. (3 marks)

50. Explain how PPE should be stored and why. (4 marks)

51. Give two reasons why we should not kill wild animals that eat crops. (2 marks)

52. Describe how to boil eggs. (4 marks)

53. A school wants to make compost from kitchen and garden wastes. Write a plan with the materials, the place, the steps and the safety measures. (5 marks)

54. Give three mistakes to avoid when sowing tiny seeds. (3 marks)

55. Name two types of tacking stitches and describe each. (3 marks)

56. List the tools and materials needed for tacking. (3 marks)

57. Describe how to plant a fruit seedling. (4 marks)

58. Why is tacking better than pins alone? (2 marks)

59. Explain four benefits of conserving fuel. (4 marks)

60. State two safety rules when making a scarecrow. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — About as high as your chest
   A heap that is too low loses heat and one that is too high is hard to turn.

2. A — To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   Dirt would clog the tiny holes.

3. C — Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
   Drip irrigation gives small amounts of water directly at the roots.

4. D — So water flows down through the pipe
   A raised container gives water the push to flow down.

5. B — Early morning or late afternoon
   The sun is less hot, so less water evaporates.

6. A — It loses a lot of heat to the air
   Open fires waste heat.

7. A — It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   Less heat escapes so less fuel is used.

8. C — Firmly fixed in the ground so it does not fall
   A loose pole falls in the wind.

9. C — Dry grass
   Dry grass is light and easy to use.

10. A — A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   A scarecrow frightens away birds and other animals.

11. A — Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   Poaching is against the law.

12. D — Young shoots of vegetables
   Hares nibble young plants.

13. A — About 1 cm
   The smaller the seed, the shallower it should be sown.

14. D — Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   Tiny seeds have little food and are weak.

15. B — To spread them thinly and evenly
   Sand helps prevent clumps of seeds.

16. B — It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   Mulch protects the surface.

17. B — Weeds take water and food from the plants
   Weeds compete with the crop.

18. B — An animal kept and cared for by people
   Domestic animals depend on people for food, water and shelter.

19. B — Wool sheep
   Some sheep breeds have wool.

20. C — Calf
   A calf is a young cow or bull.

21. B — To kill germs
   Boiling makes it safe.

22. B — Cooking oil
   Oils give a lot of energy.

23. D — Beans
   Beans have protein.

24. A — Orange
   Fruits are protective foods.

25. A — Too much oil is not good for health
   Too much oil can harm health.

26. C — A saucepan with a lid
   A saucepan holds water.

27. C — Diarrhoea
   Germs on hands can get into the mouth.

28. A — Dust, sweep, mop
   Dust falls, so dust before sweeping.

29. C — Turning used material into something new
   Recycling reuses materials.

30. B — It traps the dust
   Damp cloths hold dust.

31. B — Gloves
   Gloves protect from germs and cuts.

32. B — Vegetable peelings
   Organic waste rots.

33. B — In an airy, shady place
   Gentle drying protects the shoes.

34. C — Pull them off from the wrist so the dirty outside does not touch skin
   This prevents germs touching the skin.

35. D — Tell a teacher or an adult
   Damaged PPE may not protect you.

36. C — Store them away from small children
   Keep them safe.

37. D — Cotton
   Cotton is easy to handle.

38. C — Tell the teacher and wash with soap and water
   Clean the wound.

39. B — A handkerchief
   A handkerchief is an easy first item.

40. A — Thimble
   A thimble protects the finger.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds, hares, squirrels, monkeys (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct animal.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Soil grows our food, and if it is washed away or made poor the crops will fail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soil grows food, 1 mark for erosion or loss of plant food.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins that fight illness, fibre that helps digestion and water that keeps the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash with soap and water, rinse well and dry in the sun to help kill germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is cutting off dead, weak or crossing branches so that light and air can reach the plant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cutting, 1 mark for the purpose.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping the home and its surroundings clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for the home.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make tiny holes in the cap, fill the bottle with clean water, bury the neck upside down near the plant, press soil around it and refill when empty.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for holes in cap, 1 mark for placing near plant, 1 mark for filling and refilling.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mutton, wool (some breeds), skins, manure, income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean and dry, in a cupboard, rack or clean box, so it does not grow mould or spread germs, and labelled so it is used by the owner.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for storing, 2 marks for reasons.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: They are part of nature and biodiversity, and they help in other ways such as pollinating and eating pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, boil gently for about 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: peelings, leaves, grass. Place: shaded, well-drained, near the garden. Steps: sticks, layers, water, cover, turn. Safety: gloves, wash hands, keep children away from the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 for place, 2 for steps, 1 for safety.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Leaving big lumps in the seedbed, sowing too deep, sowing too thick without thinning, or watering strongly (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking has equal stitches and gaps; long and short tacking has a long stitch followed by a short stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name and 1 for correct descriptions.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Needle, thread, scissors, ruler or tape measure, chalk, pins, cloth, thimble (any correct materials).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water the seedling; remove the bag carefully; place at the same depth in the hole; fill with soil and firm; water and mulch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Pins can slip or prick, tacking holds cloth firmly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Saves trees and forests, saves money, reduces smoke and illness, saves time looking for firewood.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult to help with sharp or heavy work; do not use wire or broken glass; wear gloves for rough poles (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.
